clue.text: He produced a major suit honour in 1834

definitions.text: He produced a major suit honour in 1834

parts.words: He produced a major suit honour in 1834
parts.note: a major suit in bridge is spades and an honour card is a queen, so the clue describes the writer of the 1834 story The Queen of Spades

explanation.surface: A card player claims to have turned up a high trump in a game played back in 1834.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced' reads like laying down a card at bridge, but it means wrote: the Russian poet's 1834 tale is The Queen of Spades.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian poet wrote the short story The Queen of Spades, published in 1834.

clue.text: Hanoi epic about birthplace of Dido

indicators.note: about here means turned around and rearranged, so the letters of the two words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An epic poem from Hanoi tells of the queen's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it signals that HANOI and EPIC are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido, queen of Carthage, was a princess of Tyre, the chief city of the ancient Levantine coastal land.

clue.text: Tennessee Williams's airport priest

parts.note: the defrocked Reverend in The Night of the Iguana shares his surname with an Irish airport near Limerick

explanation.surface: A clergyman from a Tennessee Williams play is found at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reverend Lawrence in The Night of the Iguana bears the name of the international airport in County Clare, Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The disgraced clergyman of The Night of the Iguana has the same name as the Irish river and its airport.

clue.text: Princess of France's attendant who termed her lover's verses "Vilely compiled, profound simplicity"

definitions.text: Princess of France's attendant who termed her lover's verses "Vilely compiled, profound simplicity"

parts.words: Princess of France's attendant who termed her lover's verses "Vilely compiled, profound simplicity"
parts.note: in Love's Labour's Lost the Princess of France has ladies in waiting, and one mocks the poem sent her by Dumain in these words

explanation.surface: A lady in waiting scorns the clumsy love poetry of her suitor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Love's Labour's Lost this lady attends the Princess and is wooed by Dumain.

clue.text: "Stooping her fair pinnacles of hair, stooping, her tortoise comb showed" (James Joyce, Ulysses)

definitions.text: "Stooping her fair pinnacles of hair, stooping, her tortoise comb showed" (James Joyce, Ulysses)

parts.words: "Stooping her fair pinnacles of hair, stooping, her tortoise comb showed" (James Joyce, Ulysses)
parts.note: a quotation from Ulysses with its last word left out: the solver supplies the part of the neck the stooping barmaid shows

explanation.surface: A line from Joyce's Ulysses describing a barmaid bending forward, comb visible in her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word follows 'showed' in Joyce's description of a barmaid in the Sirens episode.
explanation.definitionFit: When a woman stoops with her hair piled up, the back of her neck is what shows beneath the comb.

clue.text: English dramatist suggests Bronteé adaptation with new ending

indicators.note: an adaptation of a novel reworks it, so the letters of the novelist's name are rearranged

parts.note: the novelist's surname, printed with a stray accent, supplies six letters
N is the standard abbreviation for new, and ending places it at the close

explanation.surface: A playwright hints that he has adapted a Brontë novel and given it a fresh finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bronteé' is the newspaper's rendering of Brontë; the accent adds no letter. 'adaptation' rearranges BRONTE into BRENTO, and 'new ending' adds N last.
explanation.definitionFit: Howard Brenton is a British playwright, author of The Romans in Britain.

clue.text: Nine barred unexpectedly from order

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters turn up in an unforeseen arrangement

explanation.surface: Nine people are surprisingly excluded from a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' and 'order' suggest exclusion from a group, but NINE and BARRED are simply rearranged, and 'order' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cistercian monks are often named for St Bernard of Clairvaux, so this is the name of a monastic order.

clue.text: Muse reveals some seer a total loss

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so a run of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: A goddess of inspiration shows that a prophet was completely ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: She is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Possibly redirect our hate to early ecologist

indicators.note: to redirect is to send a different way, and possibly marks the result as one arrangement among many

explanation.surface: Perhaps we should turn our hostility towards a pioneering environmentalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly redirect' rearranges OUR and HATE together.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Walden wrote on nature and wilderness long before environmental science existed.

clue.text: Poet offers opposite answers

parts.note: the negative reply to a question
the positive reply, the opposite of the negative one

explanation.surface: A poet gives contradictory responses.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both pieces: the two opposite answers to a question, in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English writer of verse, best known for The Highwayman.

clue.text: Love some of Bridget Riley's work

parts.note: love is a score of zero in tennis, written as the letter O
some, as in a portion, means part

explanation.surface: A fan says they love a few of a famous painter's pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridget Riley is the British painter famous for black-and-white optical illusion canvases.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget Riley is the leading British exponent of the optical-illusion style of abstract painting.

clue.text: Mountainous area revealed by Virgil

parts.note: in Dante's Divine Comedy the poet Virgil guides Dante up the great mountain of purification in the second book

explanation.surface: A guidebook writer shows readers a stretch of mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Divine Comedy, Virgil leads Dante through Hell and then up the mountain where souls are cleansed before Heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante pictures the place of purification after death as a mountain, which Virgil shows him.

clue.text: Bishop included among high churchmen in Ian Fleming's work

indicators.note: included among signals a run of letters sitting inside the words that follow

parts.words: high churchmen in Ian Fleming's work

explanation.surface: A bishop appears among the clergy in one of Ian Fleming's novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included among' points to a run spanning 'churchmen in Ian'.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ninian was an early missionary bishop who brought Christianity to the southern Picts of Scotland.

clue.text: Siege weapon creator in work (with English content) on Arcadian piper

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the preceding piece

parts.note: Pan, the goat god of Arcadia, played the pan pipes

indicators.note: content means held inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: opus is Latin for a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: The man behind a siege engine appears in a work about the pipe-playing god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' means contained, not satisfied. Panopeus fathered Epeius, maker of the wooden horse; Pan is the god of Arcadia, the pastoral heartland of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Panopeus was the father of Epeius, who built the wooden horse used to take Troy.

clue.text: He was overjoyed to find that his wife, although on pleasure bent, had a frugal mind

definitions.text: He was overjoyed to find that his wife, although on pleasure bent, had a frugal mind

parts.words: He was overjoyed to find that his wife, although on pleasure bent, had a frugal mind
parts.note: this paraphrases Cowper's comic ballad about a London linen draper, whose wife 'though on pleasure she was bent, had a frugal mind'

explanation.surface: A husband is delighted that his fun-loving wife is careful with money.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cowper's ballad tells of a draper's anniversary outing; the line about his wife's frugal mind is quoted almost directly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper's ballad hero is the linen draper whose thrifty wife plans their outing to Edmonton.

clue.text: Shelley's patricide from Saracen city

indicators.note: from here means taken out of the following words, as a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A father-killer in Shelley's work came from a Muslim city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes a run spanning 'Saracen city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's verse tragedy is named for the Roman family whose daughter Beatrice had her father killed.

clue.text: Swedish-born artist in ancient fortress

parts.note: olden means of old times, ancient
a burg is a fortified town or castle

explanation.surface: A painter born in Sweden works in an old castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Claes Oldenburg, the pop sculptor of giant everyday objects, was born in Stockholm.

clue.text: It bore stamps of both Watt and Auden

definitions.text: It bore stamps of both Watt and Auden

parts.words: It bore stamps of both Watt and Auden
parts.note: a postal train carries stamped letters, while a film bears the stamp of its director Harry Watt and its verse writer Auden

explanation.surface: Something carried postage stamps marked with two famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stamps' means both postage stamps and the mark of a maker: the 1936 documentary about a postal train was directed by Harry Watt with verse by W. H. Auden.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1936 GPO documentary about the overnight postal train had Watt as director and Auden's verse.

clue.text: Hamlet abandoned by artisan poet?

parts.note: a hamlet is a village and abandoned means deserted, recalling the poem The Deserted Village; the poet's surname is also a craftsman in precious metal

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince is dropped by a craftsman who writes verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests Shakespeare, but a hamlet is a small village: Oliver Goldsmith wrote The Deserted Village, and his surname is a trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith wrote The Deserted Village, and his surname names a craftsman in precious metal.

clue.text: He made a great sacrifice on behalf of Greek shipping

definitions.text: He made a great sacrifice on behalf of Greek shipping

parts.words: He made a great sacrifice on behalf of Greek shipping
parts.note: the leader of the Greek fleet sacrificed his daughter Iphigenia so the ships could sail to Troy

explanation.surface: A shipowner gave up a great deal for the good of the Greek merchant fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek shipping' sounds like a modern shipping magnate's business, but it is the fleet held at Aulis until Iphigenia was sacrificed.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Mycenae offered his own daughter to Artemis to win winds for the fleet bound for Troy.

clue.text: Son of Perseus and Lesbian lyric poet

explanation.surface: A hero's son is also a poet from Lesbos.
explanation.definitionFit: Two bearers of one name: a child of Perseus and Andromeda, and the poet of Mytilene contemporary with Sappho.

clue.text: Novelist makes comeback in ingenious logogriph

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the letters found are read backwards
in points to a run of letters sitting inside the following words

explanation.surface: A writer returns in a clever word puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds LOGOG at the start of 'logogriph', and 'makes comeback' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the Russian author of Dead Souls.

clue.text: Trumpeter recorded at Colorado city by Oliver Madox Brown

definitions.text: Trumpeter recorded at Colorado city by Oliver Madox Brown

parts.words: Trumpeter recorded at Colorado city by Oliver Madox Brown
parts.note: the archangel who sounds the last trumpet, joined to the state capital of Colorado, gives the title of Oliver Madox Brown's novel

explanation.surface: A trumpet player was recorded in a Colorado city by a named musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorded' suggests a studio, but it means written down: Oliver Madox Brown's novel is Gabriel Denver, the archangel's name plus Colorado's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The archangel blows the trumpet of judgment, and the novelist's hero is Gabriel Denver.

clue.text: Shining priestess destined to care for Paduan girl

definitions.text: destined to care for Paduan girl

parts.note: lucent means bright or shining
Io was a priestess of Hera loved by Zeus

explanation.surface: A radiant priestess is fated to look after a girl from Padua.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Taming of the Shrew the young suitor wins Bianca, Baptista's daughter in Padua.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's suitor wins the hand of Bianca, the younger Paduan daughter in The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Forgetfulness seen in ballet hero, entering late

indicators.note: seen in means visible within the following words, as a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A dancer playing the lead comes on late, having forgotten his cue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' finds the run spanning 'ballet hero'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the river of the underworld whose water makes the dead forget their lives.

clue.text: His traveller was unlucky

parts.note: the Elizabethan writer's picaresque novel is The Unfortunate Traveller

explanation.surface: A man's travelling companion had bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlucky' stands for 'unfortunate': Thomas Nashe wrote The Unfortunate Traveller (1594).
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Nashe wrote The Unfortunate Traveller, an early English picaresque novel.

clue.text: Dog ends said to identify animal painter

indicators.note: said signals that the word is spoken, its sound giving the answer

parts.note: dog-ends are cigarette ends, also called stubs

explanation.surface: Cigarette ends are supposedly a clue to the identity of a painter of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog ends' is British slang for cigarette butts; 'said' gives the sound of STUBS. George Stubbs painted horses.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was the eighteenth-century English painter of horses such as Whistlejacket.

clue.text: At the start of last year, no-one doubted name of the authors of Middletown

definitions.text: name of the authors of Middletown

indicators.note: at the start of picks the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Last year nobody questioned who wrote a classic of American sociology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the start of' takes the first letters of 'last year, no-one doubted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert and Helen Lynd wrote Middletown (1929), a study of Muncie, Indiana.

clue.text: Somewhat Besantine doctrine associated with the new psychology

definitions.text: Somewhat Besantine doctrine associated with the new psychology

parts.words: Somewhat Besantine doctrine associated with the new psychology
parts.note: Annie Besant led the mystical society founded by Blavatsky, whose doctrine is meant, linked with early twentieth-century psychology

explanation.surface: A creed somewhat like Annie Besant's is tied to modern psychology.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie Besant was president of the Theosophical Society, whose mystical teaching drew on spiritualist and psychological ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Besant was the leading figure of the mystical movement founded by Madame Blavatsky.

clue.text: Entrance I employ to discover Hindu goddess

parts.note: an adit is an entrance to a mine

explanation.surface: Through a doorway I find a Hindu deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Aditi is the Vedic mother of the gods in Hindu belief.

clue.text: Sculptor to record beer mug

parts.note: EP stands for extended-play record
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A sculptor is set to record a beer tankard.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein was a modernist sculptor of works such as Rock Drill.

clue.text: Tom Jones featured this treacherous character

explanation.surface: A singer performed a song about a deceitful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Jones here is the Welsh singer, not Fielding's novel: his 1968 hit is named for the Biblical betrayer of Samson.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer's hit song shares its name with the Philistine woman who betrayed Samson.
